text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London edged slightly higher during the evening trade, continuing the pattern of narrow-range movements, traders said. Spread business largely dominated trading throughout, with little emerging from the physical sector. August finished at $310.80 a tonne, up $1.60 from Friday, while October was $0.60 higher at $305.30 a tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed moderately weaker as players remained focused on the nearby switch, dealers said. Prices climbed slightly higher on the open amid trade and commission house buying, but quickly eased below unchanged in the slight correction from Friday's rally. Spot May settled 0.05 cent lower at 11.24 cents/lb, while the benchmark July contract ended down 0.01 cent at 11.08 cents/lb. The outer months closed unchanged to 0.03 cent firmer.

Most active July is expected to maintain support at 11.00 cents amid talk of buying from Russia. While dealers agreed that the rumors probably came from business done last week, they said it could provide support to the market in the near term. Resistance was pegged at 11.18 cents in July.

CHINA - Sugar production in March 1997 amounted to 1.121 mn tonnes, raw value, up slightly from last year's 1.109 mn tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the first seven months of 1996/97 (September/March) up to 6.732 mn tonnes against 6.172 mn tonnes in 1995/96.
Total output in 1995/96 reached 6.770 mn tonnes compared to 5.901 mn tonnes in 1994/95 and 6.547 mn tonnes in 1993/94. The crushing season in China will draw to a close in April.

GERMANY - Sugar imports in December 1996 amounted to 25,409 tonnes, raw value, up from 18,634 tonnes in December 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first quarter of 1996/97 (October/December) up to 70,045 tonnes against 54,224 tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 206,911 tonnes against 225,848 tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of origin in October/December 1996 were France with 50,145 tonnes whites against 40,251 tonnes and the Netherlands with 5,442 tonnes against 4,359 tonnes. Sugar exports in December 1996 amounted to 178,657 tonnes, down from 182,961 tonnes in December 1995. This brought cumulative exports in October/December 1996/97 up to 536,711 tonnes compared to 552,611 tonnes in 1995/96.

Total exports in 1995/96 reached 1.316 mn tonnes against 1.452 mn tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in October/December 1996 were Belgium-Luxembourg with 89,636 tonnes whites against 61,319 tonnes, Italy with 80,990 tonnes, up from 23,034 tonnes, the United Arab Emirates with 57,967 tonnes, down from 74,687 tonnes and Switzerland with 28,897 tonnes compared to 35,944 tonnes.

IRELAND - Sugar exports in November 1996 reached 5,657 tonnes, raw value, down from 12,121 tonnes in November 1995. This brought cumulative exports in October/November 1996 up to 10,524 tonnes against 16,723 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 74,907 tonnes compared to 56,773 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of destination in October/November 1996 was the United Kingdom with 9,561 tonnes whites against 10,674 tonnes.

BRAZIL - The head of the Sugar and Fuel Alcohol Department at the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Tourism, Pedro Cabral, has issued a tentative 1997/98 (May/April) cane production figure of 310 mn tonnes, up about 8.4 per cent versus the previous year. A meeting is planned for April 25, at which the figure will be examined. The meeting will likely provide information regarding the official new-season sugar plan.
